#!/bin/sh
# Prikk installer.
#
# Generated by `prikk-release-policy generate-installer` at release time and published as a
# release asset (never committed as a tracked .sh file) -- see docs/src/guide/install.md.
#
# A passing checksum here proves this download matches what the release page published; it does
# not prove *who* published it. In v0 one maintainer key signs every release tag; release-signers.toml
# is empty because no multi-signer policy exists yet -- see the release, versioning, and compatibility
# reference for the full statement. This script never claims more than that.
#
# Usage:
#   curl -fsSL https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh
#   curl -fsSL https://github.com/REPO_SLUG/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh -s -- --version X.Y.Z
#
# Environment overrides (equivalent to the flags above):
#   PRIKK_INSTALL_VERSION   version tag to install, default "latest"
#   PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR       install directory, default "$HOME/.local/bin"

set -eu

repo="REPO_SLUG"
version="${PRIKK_INSTALL_VERSION:-latest}"
install_dir="${PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR:-$HOME/.local/bin}"

while [ "$#" -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --version)
      version="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --prefix)
      install_dir="$2"
      shift 2
      ;;
    *)
      echo "prikk-install: unrecognized argument: $1" >&2
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
done

os="$(uname -s)"
arch="$(uname -m)"

case "$os" in
  Linux)
    case "$arch" in
      x86_64) target="x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
      aarch64) target="aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu" ;;
      *)
        echo "prikk-install: no prebuilt binary for Linux/$arch" >&2
        echo "prikk-install: try 'cargo install prikk' instead" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
    ;;
  Darwin)
    case "$arch" in
      arm64) target="aarch64-apple-darwin" ;;
      *)
        echo "prikk-install: no prebuilt binary for macOS/$arch (only Apple Silicon ships one)" >&2
        echo "prikk-install: try 'cargo install prikk' instead" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
    ;;
  MINGW* | MSYS* | CYGWIN*)
    echo "prikk-install: this script does not support Windows -- it is a POSIX shell script" >&2
    echo "prikk-install: run the Windows installer instead:" >&2
    echo "prikk-install:   irm https://github.com/$repo/releases/latest/download/install.ps1 | iex" >&2
    echo "prikk-install: or download prikk-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip from the release page by hand," >&2
    echo "prikk-install: or run 'cargo install prikk'" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "prikk-install: unsupported platform: $os/$arch" >&2
    echo "prikk-install: try 'cargo install prikk', or build from source (see the install guide)" >&2
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

if [ -n "${PRIKK_INSTALL_BASE_URL:-}" ]; then
  # Undocumented for ordinary use; exists so this script's own download-verify-extract logic can
  # be tested against a fixture server instead of the real release page.
  base_url="$PRIKK_INSTALL_BASE_URL"
elif [ "$version" = "latest" ]; then
  base_url="https://github.com/$repo/releases/latest/download"
else
  base_url="https://github.com/$repo/releases/download/$version"
fi

asset="prikk-$target.tar.gz"
checksum_tool=""
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  checksum_tool="sha256sum"
elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  checksum_tool="shasum"
else
  echo "prikk-install: neither sha256sum nor shasum is available; refusing to install unverified" >&2
  exit 1
fi

work_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$work_dir"
}
trap cleanup EXIT INT TERM

echo "prikk-install: downloading $asset ($version, $target)"
curl -fsSL "$base_url/$asset" -o "$work_dir/$asset"
curl -fsSL "$base_url/$asset.sha256" -o "$work_dir/$asset.sha256"

echo "prikk-install: verifying checksum"
if [ "$checksum_tool" = "sha256sum" ]; then
  if ! (cd "$work_dir" && sha256sum -c "$asset.sha256") >/dev/null; then
    echo "prikk-install: checksum verification failed; refusing to install" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
else
  if ! (cd "$work_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c "$asset.sha256") >/dev/null; then
    echo "prikk-install: checksum verification failed; refusing to install" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
fi

echo "prikk-install: extracting"
tar -xzf "$work_dir/$asset" -C "$work_dir"

if [ ! -f "$work_dir/prikk" ]; then
  echo "prikk-install: extracted archive did not contain a prikk binary" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$install_dir"
mv "$work_dir/prikk" "$install_dir/prikk"
chmod +x "$install_dir/prikk"

echo "prikk-install: installed to $install_dir/prikk"

# 0.57.0 item 5b/5c: the licence files travel with the binary. Where they go is chosen so that
# uninstall.sh can leave the file system as it found it:
#   - beside the install directory, in <parent>/share/licenses/prikk, when the directory is named `bin`
#     and <parent>/share already exists (the default $HOME/.local/bin on an ordinary system: this is
#     where /usr/bin has /usr/share/licenses/prikk). Only `prikk` (and `licenses`, if it is missing)
#     is created, both removed again when empty; `share` existed first and is never removed;
#   - otherwise inside the directory the user named, in <install dir>/share/licenses/prikk, so that
#     nothing is created outside it (`--prefix ~/bin` must not make ~/share). All three levels are
#     ours and are removed again, innermost first, when empty.
# uninstall.sh looks in both places, from the same --prefix / PRIKK_INSTALL_DIR.
licence_dir="$install_dir/share/licenses/prikk"
if [ "$(basename "$install_dir")" = "bin" ] && [ -d "$(dirname "$install_dir")/share" ]; then
  licence_dir="$(dirname "$install_dir")/share/licenses/prikk"
fi
for licence_file in LICENSE THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES; do
  if [ -f "$work_dir/$licence_file" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$licence_dir"
    mv "$work_dir/$licence_file" "$licence_dir/$licence_file"
    echo "prikk-install: installed $licence_dir/$licence_file"
  else
    echo "prikk-install: this archive has no $licence_file (releases before 0.57.0 ship neither licence file)" >&2
  fi
done

path_marker_begin="# >>> prikk installer >>>"
path_marker_end="# <<< prikk installer <<<"

case ":$PATH:" in
  *":$install_dir:"*)
    on_path=1
    ;;
  *)
    on_path=0
    ;;
esac

if [ "$on_path" -eq 0 ]; then
  shell_name="$(basename "${SHELL:-}")"
  rc_file=""
  case "$shell_name" in
    zsh) rc_file="$HOME/.zshrc" ;;
    bash) rc_file="$HOME/.bashrc" ;;
    *) rc_file="" ;;
  esac

  # The installer only adds a block to a startup file that already exists: it never creates one, so an
  # uninstall can leave the file system as it was. When the file is missing it prints the line instead.
  if [ -n "$rc_file" ] && [ ! -f "$rc_file" ]; then
    echo "prikk-install: $rc_file does not exist, so it was not created; add this line to your shell's"
    echo "prikk-install: startup file yourself:"
    echo "prikk-install:   export PATH=\"$install_dir:\$PATH\""
  elif [ -n "$rc_file" ]; then
    if grep -qF "$path_marker_begin" "$rc_file" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "prikk-install: $rc_file already has a PATH entry from a previous install"
    else
      # The literal $PATH below is meant to land in the rc file unexpanded, so it re-evaluates at
      # every future shell startup rather than freezing today's PATH value.
      # shellcheck disable=SC2016
      printf '\n%s\nexport PATH="%s:$PATH"\n%s\n' \
        "$path_marker_begin" "$install_dir" "$path_marker_end" >> "$rc_file"
      echo "prikk-install: added $install_dir to PATH in $rc_file (restart your shell, or run: . $rc_file)"
      echo "prikk-install: note for macOS Terminal: it starts a login shell, which reads ~/.bash_profile," >&2
      echo "prikk-install: not ~/.bashrc, unless your ~/.bash_profile already sources it" >&2
    fi
  else
    echo "prikk-install: could not detect your shell (\$SHELL=${SHELL:-<unset>}); add this to your"
    echo "prikk-install: shell's startup file yourself:"
    echo "prikk-install:   export PATH=\"$install_dir:\$PATH\""
  fi
fi

echo "prikk-install: done. Run 'prikk --version' (after opening a new shell, if PATH was just updated)."
echo "prikk-install: this checksum proves the download matches what the release page published;"
echo "prikk-install: it does not prove who published it. In v0 one maintainer key signs every release"
echo "prikk-install: tag; release-signers.toml is empty because no multi-signer policy exists yet."
